item.title: Cisse commemorated in painting at Gozo basilica
item.description: St Georges Basilica in Victoria, Gozo, has shared a message on racism, justice and compassion alongside photographs of a painting commemorating Lassana Cisse inside the church, as the murder trial continues. The artwork forms part of the basilicas Fejn Hu Ħuk? project exploring the Works of Mercy through art. The church called for justice without revenge, stressed that the accused are presumed innocent until proven guilty, and said the tragedy also affected migrants who may now feel unsafe, police and the families of those accused.

item.title: Woman given three years probation over string of robberies
item.description: Shirley Al Omar of Mosta was placed on three years probation with three years treatment after the court accepted her guilty plea to a series of robberies committed in 2020, when she accompanied by her 12-year-old son knocked on the doors of elderly victims asking for money and fled once the victims realised they had been robbed. The magistrate noted significant progress since the offences, including overcoming drug addiction, finding work and living a stable life, and ordered a 2,000 personal guarantee that she not approach her victims for a year.

item.title: Worker crushed to death by materials falling from a tower crane at Ħal Far site
item.description: A 51-year-old Turkish construction worker from Mqabba died on Saturday after materials being lifted by a tower crane fell on him at a construction site in the Ħal Far industrial estate. The accident happened at around 1.15pm near the Playmobil factory. Police said the man was operating the crane and was found dead on site; earlier reports suggested he had fallen from scaffolding, but police later clarified he was struck by falling materials. A medical team and Civil Protection Department personnel attended. Magistrate Joe Mifsud has opened an inquiry, with the police, the Occupational Health and Safety Authority and the Building and Construction Authority investigating.

item.title: Bedingfield says man removed from Floriana subway had been given shelter
item.description: Home Affairs Minister Glenn Bedingfield said the man removed by police from the Triq SantAnna underpass in Floriana had been given shelter, adding that it was his job to maintain order and that people found sleeping rough should be treated with dignity. The minister had posted a photo on Facebook saying the subway is not meant for sleeping, which drew racist backlash and criticism from academic Michelle Attard Tonna, who said posting the image only incited further hatred. Bedingfield said he does not like seeing racist comments and that security and personal dignity are his responsibility.

item.title: Pharmacies to open on Sunday 25 October, health centres on emergency duty
item.description: A list of pharmacies open across Malta and Gozo on Sunday 25 October was published, with one dispensary serving each locality grouping, running from Valletta and Floriana through to Marsalforn and Xagħra. The mobile blood donation unit will be stationed in Mqabba beside the parish church from 8.30am to 1pm, with blood donors asked to bring identification cards. The health centres in Mqabba, Raħal Ġdid and Floriana will also open for emergencies 24 hours a day for the whole week.

item.title: Courts powerless to punish those pardoned over disability benefits racket, court says
item.description: Hundreds of people pardoned over Maltas disability benefits racket cannot be hauled back before the courts if they break the terms of their deal, a spate of rulings has made clear. In the latest decision, on Thursday, Magistrate Caroline Farrugia Frendo closed the case against a woman who had admitted defrauding social security, relying on a 2002 Constitutional Court judgment that places presidential pardons beyond the reach of any court. The Criminal Code is silent on those pardoned before sentencing, leaving the power to withdraw a pardon with the President alone.

item.title: Abela represents Malta as Hungary marks 70 years since the 1956 uprising
item.description: Foreign Minister Carmelo Abela represented Malta at events marking the 70th anniversary of the Hungarian Revolution of 1956, attended by dignitaries from more than 40 countries. He met Péter Magyar, Hungarian President András Baka and parliamentary speaker Ágnes Forsthoffer, as well as European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, who addressed a ceremonial parliamentary session. Magyar said Hungary wanted to be a reliable EU partner and would no longer drift between East and West.

item.title: Court says bank should have stepped in after man lost 70,000 in deepfake Abela scam
item.description: The Court of Appeal said Bank of Valletta must partly compensate a 45-year-old man who lost about 70,000 in eight days in November 2023, after falling for a pig-butchering scam built on a fake Facebook video of Prime Minister Robert Abela promoting an investment scheme. The man, who had barely used his account before, was coached by a trader on WhatsApp and used remote-access software to hand over security codes. The court found the bank failed in its duty to monitor his payments and flag that something was badly amiss.

item.title: Cutajar reports TikTok user who praised Cisse’s alleged killers
item.description: Equality Minister Rosianne Cutajar has reported to the police a man who praised two former soldiers accused of murdering Lassane Cisse because he was black. The comment, posted under a Times of Malta video about the 2019 killing, said the alleged shooters were defending their country against trash black people and that it was a pity they killed only one of three men. Cutajars intervention came hours after the trial of one of the accused, Lorin Scicluna, opened with testimony naming his friend as the shooter.

item.title: Ten years on, Malta remembers the plane crash that killed five
item.description: A small Fairchild Merlin IV operated by CAE Aviation crashed into the dunes at Ħal Safi shortly after taking off from Malta International Airport ten years ago today, killing all five people on board two crew and three officials from the French defence ministry. The aircraft was on a surveillance mission linked to a French operation against Mediterranean trafficking routes and had been airborne for about ten seconds. Reports at the time said Frontex had initially been believed to have personnel aboard, a claim the agency denied.

item.title: Scicluna told police his friend fired the shot that killed Lassane Cisse, jury hears
item.description: Former soldier Lorin Scicluna told the court that his friend Francesco Fenech was the one who fired the shot that killed Lassane Cisse, the 42-year-old Ivorian worker shot dead in Birżebbuġa in April 2019. CID officer Jeffrey Gerada told jurors that Scicluna was very nervous and took police to various locations he mentioned while under interrogation, including an Attard pastizzi shop where he worked part-time and where he said he had lent his car to a Libyan man. Scicluna, who pleads not guilty, faces nine charges and is also accused of the attempted murder of two other black men shot in the same incident.

item.title: Momentum urges EU action on housing, AI and social media at EDP congress
item.description: Momentum Secretary General Mark Camilleri Gambin, speaking at the European Democratic Party congress in Athens, called for greater European coordination on capital taxation, stronger accountability for social media platforms and measures to prepare workers for artificial intelligence. He said growth that people cannot feel is not prosperity and that young Maltese couples unable to afford homes showed something had gone wrong. He condemned looting, arson and attacks on workers while urging that peaceful protesters grievances over housing, prices, schools and hospitals should not be overshadowed by the actions of a minority.

item.title: BCAs new mascot designed by a student to promote construction careers
item.description: An ant designed by a Maltese school student will become the face of a Building and Construction Authority campaign introducing children to construction careers. Jamie Casha of the Malta Visual and Performing Arts School chose an ant to symbolise strength and designed its hands to represent the practical skills needed to use construction tools. A 3D model of the winning design was presented to Infrastructure Minister Jonathan Attard and BCA CEO Roderick Bonnici.

item.title: Turkish health delegation visits Gozo General Hospital
item.description: A delegation led by Turkeys deputy health minister Şuayip Birinci visited Gozo General Hospital during a two-day official visit to Malta. Parliamentary Secretary for Active Ageing Deo Debattista said the visit was intended to strengthen cooperation between the two countries in healthcare. Turkish officials were given an overview of the hospitals facilities and medical services, and the two sides exchanged knowledge on healthcare investment and developing medical services.

item.title: EU commissioners inspect Nadur school after 10m of upgrades
item.description: European Commissioners Piotr Serafin and Glenn Micallef visited Nadur Primary School in Gozo to see how EU funding has improved its facilities, accessibility and energy efficiency. The school, funded through Maltas Recovery and Resilience Plan and the EUs NextGenerationEU programme, cut its primary energy demand by 82.6% and moved from an energy efficiency rating of Class D to Class A. The works formed part of a wider 10 million allocation that also included Għaxaq Primary School.

item.title: Man walks free after his brother drops the arson case
item.description: Errol Grech walked out of court a free man on Friday after his brother told the court he no longer wished to pursue an arson case against him. The two brothers were charged in 2019 with setting fire to a Volkswagen belonging to a third brother, Rosario Grech, in Żejtun, and Errol Grech was eventually jailed for four years. His conviction was overturned on appeal, and Magistrate Astrid May Grima upheld the victims request, ending the proceedings.

item.title: Aquilina says he is physically threatened in public
item.description: Civil society activist Robert Aquilina said he has been physically threatened and attacked in public as part of a campaign to dehumanise him, comparing it to the campaign against Daphne Caruana Galizia before she was killed. Speaking on a pre-recorded programme, he said Labour supporters have spotted him in public and moved to assault him. Last Wednesday he named the alleged creator of a derogatory AI-generated image of him as Joseph Abela, brother of former judge Toni Abela, saying the information was verified by police.

item.title: 29 years on, Għawdex marks the explosion that killed two
item.description: Twenty-nine years after an explosion in a Santa Margerita ammunition store in the limits of Munxar killed two men from the same family, the community of Sannat in Għawdex still marks the tragedy. Kelinu Azzopardi, known as il-Kappuna, aged 52, and his son-in-law Joe Grima, aged 29, died in the 10.30am blast on 23 October 1997, which was felt as far away as mainland Malta. The then prime minister Alfred Sant travelled to the site.

item.title: Government to strengthen the 1400 helpline and community health services
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Health Minister Ian Borg said the government plans further improvements to the 1400 medical helpline and primary healthcare services to direct patients to the most appropriate care and reduce pressure on Mater Dei Hospitals emergency department. Since July 2025 the 1400 service has assisted more than 59,418 people, averaging 124 patients a day. Planned changes include patient-streamlining at health centres, infrastructure and equipment upgrades, and a new digital system giving callers real-time information on waiting times.

item.title: Government to back businesses on EU competitiveness, says Azzopardi Tanti
item.description: Minister for European Funds, Social Dialogue and Consumer Protection Keith Azzopardi Tanti addressed a business breakfast marking the 30th anniversary of the Malta Business Bureau, bringing together government, industry and social partners. Discussions focused on digital innovation, adapting to environmental requirements and making EU policy take account of the conditions under which businesses operating on islands function. MBB president Raphael Aloisio said the bureaus early engagement on EU initiatives continues to deliver value for Maltese business.

item.title: Visitor centre planned at the prehistoric Baħrija site
item.description: A year after the Planning Authority rejected a residential proposal on the Baħrija plateau, a new application for a visitor and research centre in the same Bronze Age settlement zone has been submitted. Application PA/7541/26 was filed last month by the Baħrija Foundation, whose website was only registered in July and which does not appear in the Malta Business Registry. The application confirms the foundation is not the property owner but is presenting it with the owners consent.

item.title: Malta embassy in France urges vigilance ahead of demonstrations
item.description: The Embassy of Malta in France has warned Maltese nationals living in or visiting the country to be more vigilant ahead of demonstrations expected on Saturday. The embassy said the protests could cause transport disruptions, road closures and restricted access to some areas, advising nationals to avoid gatherings and allow extra time for journeys. Around 70,000 law enforcement officers are expected to be deployed as protests over the cost of living and crumbling educational infrastructure continue.

item.title: Beekeepers warn the €1m honey bee plan may not be enough
item.description: Beekeeping and environmental organisations welcomed the governments seven-measure, 1 million action plan against the Oriental hornet but warn the funding may be insufficient. They say aid for re-establishing lost colonies should be restricted to the native Maltese honey bee, Apis mellifera ruttneri, and want clarity on how the required proportion of Maltese bees will be verified. The plan also covers compensation for lost honey production and breeding programmes for the native subspecies.

item.title: Solidarjetà: foreign workers are not the cause of traffic and overdevelopment
item.description: The Solidarjetà union says Maltas traffic congestion, overdevelopment and high rents stem from poor planning and regulation rather than from foreign workers. The union, which represents migrant workers and local residents, said foreign workers are essential to healthcare, elderly care, public transport, cleaning, construction and hospitality. It asked the budget due next week to treat migrant workers with the same dignity and respect as others, warning that low wages and poor conditions harm every worker.

item.title: MFSA appoints auditors to take control of Trive’s assets
item.description: The Malta Financial Services Authority has appointed Grant Thornton to take control of the Ta Xbiex-based online trading platform Trive Financial Services, whose clients have been left unable to access their money. The Turkish-owned firm was left without a board after a spate of top-level resignations left it unable to operate; if the business cannot be salvaged, Grant Thornton will wind it up on the MFSAs instructions. The move follows a 10-year ban on shareholder Kasim Garipoglu from operating in Maltas regulated financial services sector.
item.content:encoded:
The Malta Financial Services Authority has appointed Grant Thornton to take control of the Ta Xbiex-based online trading platform Trive Financial Services, whose clients have been left unable to access their money. The Turkish-owned firm was left without a board after a spate of top-level resignations left it unable to operate; if the business cannot be salvaged, Grant Thornton will wind it up on the MFSAs instructions. The move follows a 10-year ban on shareholder Kasim Garipoglu from operating in Maltas regulated financial services sector.

Sources: The Business Picture

item.title: Femicide observatory: partners linked to 24 of 55 women killed since 1970
item.description: The Malta Observatory on Femicide says a current partner killed 24 of the 55 women it has identified as femicide victims in Malta between January 1970 and September 2026, with an ex-partner responsible for 13 more. Twenty-seven of the victims were killed in their own home, and 93% of the perpetrators were male. The figures are not official statistics, as Malta has no national femicide dataset, and the observatory compiles its count from public sources.
